questions.prompt: Through which structure does a leaf take in carbon dioxide?
questions.why: Gas exchange in plants mainly happens through stomata on the leaf.
questions.quote: Gas exchange in plants is mainly carried out through the stomata.

questions.prompt: What gas do green plants use during respiration?
questions.why: Plants use oxygen and release energy in respiration.
questions.quote: During respiration, they use oxygen and produce carbon dioxide.

questions.prompt: Under light conditions, what is the net result for carbon dioxide?
questions.why: Photosynthesis outpaces respiration, so plants take in more carbon dioxide.
questions.quote: As a result, there is a net uptake of carbon dioxide.

questions.prompt: Under dark conditions, what gas shows net uptake?
questions.why: In darkness only respiration occurs, so plants take up oxygen.
questions.quote: Therefore, there is a net release of carbon dioxide and a net uptake of oxygen.

questions.prompt: Under light conditions, what do green plants carry out?
questions.why: Both photosynthesis and respiration occur under light.
questions.quote: Under light conditions: Plants carry out both photosynthesis and respiration.

questions.prompt: Under light, how does the rate of photosynthesis compare with respiration?
questions.why: Photosynthesis runs faster under light conditions.
questions.quote: The rate of photosynthesis is higher than the rate of respiration.

questions.prompt: Under light conditions, what gas is released net by the plant?
questions.why: Plants release more oxygen from photosynthesis than they use.
questions.quote: As a result, there is a net release of oxygen.

questions.prompt: What do stomata allow gases like carbon dioxide and oxygen to do?
options: Move into or out of the leaves
questions.why: Stomata let gases enter and leave the leaf.
questions.quote: They allow gases like carbon dioxide and oxygen to move into or out of the leaves

questions.prompt: What does the net gas exchange in plants depend on?
options: The relative rates of photosynthesis and respiration
questions.why: Net gas exchange depends on the balance of the two rates.
questions.quote: The net gas exchange in plants depends on the relative rates of photosynthesis and respiration.

questions.prompt: When does respiration occur in green plants?
questions.why: Respiration happens continuously, in light and dark.
questions.quote: Respiration occurs all the time in green plants.

questions.prompt: Which colour does hydrogencarbonate indicator show at higher than normal carbon dioxide levels?
questions.why: Higher-than-normal carbon dioxide makes the indicator yellow.
questions.quote: Hydrogencarbonate indicator shows different colours at different levels of carbon dioxide.

questions.prompt: What can the data logger with an oxygen sensor measure?
questions.why: The data logger with an oxygen sensor measures oxygen content around the leaves.
questions.quote: The data logger with an oxygen sensor can measure and record the changes in oxygen content

questions.prompt: Approximately what percentage of carbon dioxide is in normal air?
questions.why: Normal air contains about 0.04% carbon dioxide.

questions.prompt: What gas do green plants use during photosynthesis?
questions.why: Plants use carbon dioxide during photosynthesis.
questions.quote: During photosynthesis, they use carbon dioxide and produce oxygen.
